title: Personal Credit Cards: bank error ground or no ground for a late fee on an autopay card
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: combining the autopay bank error test into one ground

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. It states how the autopay bank error test for a late payment fee on a card that carried an automatic payment instruction combines into a single outcome: the bank error ground, or none.

## Rule

1. The outcome is the bank error ground only when an unreversed late payment fee is found **and** every condition of the autopay bank error test holds. The test is conjunctive: one failing condition is enough to take the outcome to none.
2. When the outcome is the bank error ground, the bank failed to take the debit that autopay makes on the due date, so the fee is the bank's error, and the cardholder's courtesy allowance is neither used nor consulted.
3. When no unreversed late payment fee is found, or any condition of the test fails, this policy grounds no reversal and the outcome is none. Whether such a fee may be waived as a courtesy is then decided only under the general courtesy late fee reversal rules of Personal Credit Cards.

## Truth table

| Unreversed late payment fee found | Every condition of the autopay bank error test holds | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | bank error ground |
| yes | no, at least one fails | none |
| no | any | none |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** the courtesy allowance is checked first, or is used up, when the bank error ground applies. **Correct:** it is neither used nor consulted.
- **Wrong:** a fee that meets the whole test may be reversed as a courtesy instead. **Correct:** a fee that meets the whole test was billed contrary to the charter, and its ground is bank error.
- **Wrong:** an outcome of none means the fee can never be reversed. **Correct:** none means only that this policy grounds no reversal; the courtesy question is decided under the general courtesy rules.
- **Wrong:** most of the conditions holding is enough. **Correct:** every condition must hold.
